what: Root questions for CodeMother's trees. Three layers: Akien's cognition questions (the broad cross-domain links), the 6-Angle Novelty Matrix (graph-native operations), and coding-domain starters (depth seeds for code). Smarts come from two kinds of links: deep within a domain, and broad across domain boundaries. The cognition questions create the broad links. The coding questions seed the depth. The model handles the rest.
why: Akien 2026-07-12: 'I have figured out novelty. I not only have the questions to ask in the face of novelty. but if those fail, I have the questions to ask to sort the questions to ask. and I can do that in a graph tree.' COGNITION QUESTIONS ARE THE COMPILER — open questions compile out, these find what the contract missed. Akien 2026-09-03: domain-specific starter questions cause the appropriate accretions of nodes.

provenance.cognition_questions: Recovered from UnseenUniversity era (TheIgorsProject/.claude.old/file-history). Akien verbatim 2026-07-12 (oldest batch) + 2026-07-02 cortical-columns log (pattern-selection sequence). CC.0's function/class taxonomy is PROPOSED, not Akien's.
provenance.novelty_matrix: 2026-07-14 (Novelty.txt) + 2026-07-23 (GeiniOnNovelty.md) — Akien's verbatim questions mapped to graph operations.
provenance.coding_domain: CC-proposed 2026-09-03, directed by Akien. Boris Cherny's hat: make the illegal state unrepresentable. Approved as starting set.

cognition_questions.question: What does it mean to me?
cognition_questions.note: Distinct from 'What does that mean?' — this asks for RELEVANCE and stake, not denotation.

cognition_questions.question: What does that mean?
cognition_questions.note: The plain semantic unpack. Pairs with, but is NOT, 'what does it mean to me'.

cognition_questions.question: How must that work? / how would that have to work?
cognition_questions.note: NOT the same as 'how might that work?'. MUST reasons BACKWARD from a required outcome (constraint derivation). MIGHT reasons FORWARD into the possible (generation).

cognition_questions.question: Which choice is most in alignment with who I'd most like to be?
cognition_questions.note: The identity/telos selector. Sits INSIDE the novelty process, not outside as an ethics review — consonant with 'the core values ARE the architecture'.

cognition_questions.question: What's the first thing i say in repsonse to that?
cognition_questions.note: VERBATIM including the typo. Captures the UNEDITED first response before reasoning launders it — a probe of the model you have but cannot yet articulate.

cognition_questions.question: What looks like it would fit there?
cognition_questions.note: This IS the graph-tree lookup, in meatware: what pattern activates for this shape?

cognition_questions.question: How could we get around that?
cognition_questions.note: Generative, but bounded by a blocker — distinct from open generation.

cognition_questions.question: Where is the lever?
cognition_questions.note: Already load-bearing vocabulary in this project.

cognition_questions.question: How will us monkeys screw that up such that i get support questions?
cognition_questions.note: THE ONLY QUESTION FRAMED FROM AN EXTERNAL ACTOR'S VIEW. The IT-division bar in question form — maintainability/operability check at design time.

cognition_questions.question: which of these patterns would be best for this?
cognition_questions.note: Step 1 of a 4-step sequence from the 2026-07-02 cortical-columns log.

cognition_questions.question: does that leave any gaps?
cognition_questions.note: THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. CP1 ('I don't know') operationalized as a THINKING MOVE. Fires BEFORE committing to an answer. The organ the compiled-inference thesis requires — a teach-on-miss graph that cannot detect a miss compiles the lie in permanently.

cognition_questions.question: are there any patterns that could be trimmed to fit into that gap?
cognition_questions.note: Fires ON a detected gap: don't invent from scratch, ADAPT the nearest pattern.

cognition_questions.question: how might that work?
cognition_questions.note: AKIEN'S NUMBER ONE (his words, 2026-07-12). Forward, generative, exploratory. The counterpart to 'how MUST that work?'.

novelty_matrix.provenance: Akien 2026-07-14 (verbatim) + 2026-07-23 (GeiniOnNovelty.md, 6-Angle formalization). Questions mapped to graph operations.

from_2026_07_14.question: What need is that serving?
from_2026_07_14.note: Paired with 'how might that work?' IN THE SAME BREATH (2026-07-14).

from_2026_07_14.question: Can I get inside of it?
Can I see any experiments to perform to learn more?
from_2026_07_14.note: Forces generation of tests and probes.

six_angle_additions.question: How close is this to things I already know?
What questions could I ask that I don't have prepared that would increase my understanding?
How can I test for 'understandable closeness'?
What is the exact opposite of this behavior, and do we know how to handle that?
What is the minimum condition required for this to fail completely?
If we assume this novel behavior is a feature, what goal is it accomplishing?
six_angle_additions.graph_op: re-evaluate error payloads as intent payloads

six_angle_additions.question: What changed immediately before this novel state appeared?
six_angle_additions.graph_op: trace back along recent cycle history

six_angle_additions.question: Has this shape of novelty appeared during a similar deployment or state transition in the past?
How would a different specialized role view this?
What is the simplest way to explain this to another Igor on the Discord bus?
six_angle_additions.graph_op: hash intention+constraints for peer graph patch

coding_domain.provenance: CC-proposed 2026-09-03, directed by Akien. These seed depth within the coding domain. Boris Cherny's hat (14-16): make the illegal state unrepresentable.

questions.question: What is this code's single job, and does every line serve it?
What would break if this disappeared?
What does this code assume is true that it doesn't check?
What is the contract between this and its callers, and where is it written down?
What state does this carry between calls, and who else can see it?
What happens to this when the thing it depends on changes shape?
What would a test that could actually fail look like?
If this is wrong, how long before someone notices?
What does this code do that the name doesn't tell you?
Where does the same decision get made twice?
What measurement would tell us this is doing its job in production?
What pattern from a completely different domain would solve this more simply?
Who is the next person to touch this, and what will they misunderstand?
questions.function: human factors for code (parallel to Q-cog-009)

questions.question: What illegal state does this code allow that the structure could prevent?
questions.function: structural enforcement (Boris Cherny: make the illegal state unrepresentable)
questions.note: Law 4 turned on code — if it matters, make it physics.

questions.question: What runtime check here is doing a job the types or the schema should do?
questions.function: push enforcement earlier (Cherny: detect at compile, not at crash)

questions.question: What valid input to this function would produce nonsense?
questions.function: type hole — the shape permits what the intention forbids

questions.question: What happens when two of these run at the same time?
What does this code's error message actually tell the person who sees it?
questions.function: error path quality (Law 7: errors loud at diagnostic surfaces)

questions.question: What resource does this code hold, and what happens if it's never released?
What input to this code comes from outside the trust boundary?
